I’m sitting on my hostel bed staring at the floor, completely numb, wondering why my brain is so uniquely broken compared to everyone else.

Rejected again. That makes it 12 placement interviews in a row where I got to the final round and got ghosted or rejected. Today, my cousin posted on the family WhatsApp group about landing a 20 LPA package and my mom immediately messaged me asking why I can't just focus more. I didn't even reply. I just crawled under my blanket and I've been staring at the wall for hours, feeling like a parasite on my parents.

I messed up my gate exam prep again. This is my drop year, and I'm scoring worse in the mock tests now than I did last year. My parents took out a loan for my coaching and every time I look at my test scores, my chest tightens and I feel like throwing up. I can't face them, I can't face my teachers, and I feel like I'm just throwing their hard-earned money down the drain because I'm too stupid to crack this.

I have 4 backlogs now and the college just sent an email warning me about academic probation. I tried so hard this semester to attend lectures, but every time I sat in that hall, the anxiety of how far behind I am made me walk out and hide in the library. Now I've failed the makeup exams too. I feel like I'm stuck in a quicksand of my own failures and the more I try to pull myself out, the deeper I sink.

I just stared at the screen during the LeetCode round today and my mind went completely blank. This is the fourth coding round I've flunked this month. Everyone in my hostel wing is already placed at 12+ LPA, and I'm still struggling to reverse a linked list under pressure. I literally went to the washroom and cried because I felt like a parasitic drain on my parents who took a loan for this engineering degree. I've failed so many times now that even starting a mock test makes my chest feel tight and empty.

Third semester results just dropped and I got an F in Analog Electronics. That's my second backlog now. My CGPA has tanked to a 5.8 and my dad called me yesterday asking why my cousin got a 9.2 while I'm 'wasting his hard-earned money'. I didn't even have the courage to tell him about the backlog. I feel like a walking disappointment, and no matter how much I study, the moments I sit in that exam hall, my brain just resets to zero. I think I'm just fundamentally stupid and there's no fixing it.

Rejected again at the HR round. That’s five companies in a row where I make it to the final stage and then get ghosted or rejected. I don't know what's wrong with me—is my voice weird, am I too awkward, or can they just sense that I'm a fraud who doesn't belong there? My friends tell me 'your time will come' but it feels like empty platitudes while they post their 'Happy to share' updates on LinkedIn. I'm so exhausted of picking myself up just to get knocked down again.

I messed up the calibration on the chemistry lab equipment today and ruined the dataset for my entire group. My lab partners didn't say anything bad, but I could see the annoyance on their faces when they realized they had to stay back an extra hour. I spent the walk back to my PG calling myself a pathetic, useless idiot who can't even handle basic instructions. This keeps happening—I make one tiny mistake, panic, and then ruin everything else because I can't stop shaking.

I took a drop year to prepare for GATE, and today's mock exam score was even lower than my actual rank last year. I’ve sacrificed my social life, deleted all social media, stayed in this tiny room for 10 hours a day, and for what? My parents spent money on this coaching institute and I'm just proving that I'm a waste of investment. I look at my college friends starting their corporate jobs and I feel like an absolute ghost who got left behind in time.

Third coding round rejection this month. I literally practiced 300 LeetCode questions, but the moment the interviewer asked me to optimize my DFS solution, my brain just went completely blank. I sat there sweating, stuttering, and could barely write a line of code while they just stared at me. I'm a 3rd year CSE student with a 6.2 CGPA and everyone around me is securing high-paying summer internships while I can't even pass a basic technical interview. I feel like a massive fraud who doesn't belong in this branch at all.

I got my midterm marks back for DSA and it's another failing grade. This is my second time taking this course because I got an F last semester. I stayed up till 4 AM every night doing the practice labs, but I still couldn't even compile my code during the actual exam. My dad keeps calling to ask if I've cleared my backlogs because my cousin just got a 15 LPA job, and I can't even tell him I failed again. I just want to curl up under my desk and never come out, I'm tired of trying so hard just to fail over and over.

Failed my driving test for the fourth time today, and to make it worse, I accidentally scraped the bumper of the instructor's car while trying to parallel park. I am 22 years old and literally everyone I know can drive. My friends make jokes about picking me up, but it secretly stings so bad because I feel like an absolute child who can't master a basic life skill. I feel like my brain lacks some fundamental coordination chip that normal people have, and I'm just destined to fail at everything.

I was rejected from yet another student club today. That’s the third society that’s rejected me after the interview round this semester. I sat in the hostel common room watching everyone celebrate their inductions and write long posts on LinkedIn. I feel so invisible and useless, like I am just this background character in everyone else's successful college life who exists only to fill up the rejection statistics.

I got my GATE mock test results back and I scored in the bottom 20th percentile again. I've taken a drop year, spent my parents' hard-earned money on coaching classes, and I'm still getting worse with every single mock test. My parents call me every Sunday to ask how my preparation is going, and I just lie through my teeth because the truth is too humiliating. I have failed every major exam I've ever taken, and I'm starting to realize I'm just stupid and there is no fixing it.

I failed the Amazon OT again today. This is my 4th rejection in a row. My roommate already got placed at Adobe and his package is 25 LPA, while I can't even get past the first round of basic DSA coding runs. I literally spent the entire night debugging my Graph DFS code, only to TLE during the actual test. I feel like a complete waste of space, my dad took a loan for my college and I'm just throwing his hard-earned money down the drain.

My marksheet for the 5th semester just dropped and I got an F in Microprocessors. That makes it my third backlog in two years. Everyone in my hostel is talking about their system design prep, and here I am, begging my HOD for a re-evaluation form. I literally cannot face my parents when they call me this Sunday. I’ve tried so hard to study, but the moment I sit in the exam hall, my mind goes totally blank.

Another mock interview down and the mentor basically told me I lack communication skills and shouldn't dream of product-based companies. I've given 8 mock interviews this month and every single feedback sheet looks identical. I study the sheets, I practice in front of the mirror, and then I fail again. I'm starting to think my brain just isn't wired for this, and I'm doomed to be unemployed after spending four years here.

I messed up my core Java lab test today and the professor literally laughed when he saw my NullPointerException error. It's the third lab in a row where my output didn't compile. I see people around me writing code like they were born with a keyboard, and I can't even handle basic object-oriented concepts without choking. I spent the whole walk back to my PG crying because I'm clearly the dumbest person in this batch.

My dad called today asking if I got shortlisted for the TCS drive. I had to lie and tell him the results aren't out, because the truth is I got filtered out in the first aptitude round itself. Just like I got filtered out from Infosys last week, and Wipro before that. I can't even clear the absolute basic screening rounds. I feel like a parasite living on my parents' money, failing them over and over again.

I just flunked another DSA round. It was a simple sliding window problem and my brain just froze, giving me a massive TLE. This is the 5th rejection in a row this month while everyone in my hostel wing is posting their placement selfies and updating their LinkedIn with 'I am thrilled to announce...'. My dad called today asking if I'm even studying or just wasting his hard-earned money on coaching. I feel like a complete parasite who doesn't deserve to be in this college.

I failed M3 again. This is my third attempt at this single backlog paper and I still couldn't clear the cutoff. I had to sit in the remedial hall with the 2nd year juniors today, and the look of pity on the professor's face made me want to swallow glass. I used to be a straight-A student in school, but now I’m just a chronic failure who can't even solve a basic differential equation. I’m starting to believe that my brain is physically incapable of learning anymore.

Just got my ranks for the national mock test series and I’m still stuck at the 60th percentile. My parents took out a major personal loan to send me to this coaching center, and every time they call to ask if I've cracked the top 100, I have to lie or change the subject. I’ve given 12 mocks now and my score hasn’t shifted by even 2 marks. I’m drowning in guilt because their hard-earned money is being poured into a black hole of my absolute incompetence.

I got rejected from another walk-in drive today. They didn't even look at my resume after I failed to optimize the database query in the 10-minute screening. This is my 8th straight rejection and my CodeChef rating has dropped from 3 stars to 2 stars because of my awful contest runs. I see my classmates talking about system design and high-level architecture in the canteen, and I can't even write a clean bug-free loop without crashing my terminal. I am a joke.

I pulled all-nighters for three weeks straight, drank endless cups of black coffee, ignored my friends, and literally lived in the library to save my GPA. The results came out today and it went down from 6.2 to 5.8 because I flunked the analog electronics paper. I don’t know what else to do anymore. No matter how much sleep I sacrifice or how hard I try, I just end up failing even harder than before.
